question: Is 1000 uF added 12 V GPU slot capacitance unrealistically conservative?
intendedCards: User intends a lower-range AMD RX 5000 through RX 9000 series card; exact card and PCB variant not selected.

sources.author: PCI-SIG
sources.title: PCI Express Card Electromechanical Specification Revision 3.0
sources.scope: Generic add-in-card power-rail envelope; not a measurement or typical value for an AMD GPU.

sources.author: Analog Devices / Linear Technology
sources.scope: Independent semiconductor-vendor design guidance corroborates the original specification value.

conclusions: 1000 uF is a plausible intermediate compatibility test load, not an established typical value or a measured property of the intended GPU.
Neither GPU family nor board power rating establishes capacitance presented specifically to the slot 12 V input. Exact board topology and auxiliary-power partitioning matter.
The earlier simulation adds card capacitance to the adapter board bulk capacitance; it does not count the same board capacitor twice.
25 W initial functional power limits in CEM section 4.2 do not bound capacitor charging to 25 W or eliminate inrush stress.
Extreme preheat, full-current startup and rapid supply-collapse cases remain sensitivities, not predictions of routine cold-start operation.
The approximate AO4407A model also flags the 1000 uF capacitor-only nominal case; excluding extreme hot corners alone does not close that screening finding.
implementationPreference: Retain discrete-switch topology for fastest prototype work. Do not reintroduce an eFuse redesign merely because this approximate screen is open.
